correctness.rationale: For w>0, C1, define D_alpha y=y_prime/w on H1 functions satisfying (1-alpha)y(0)+alpha y(1)=0; direct inversion gives D_alpha^-1=T_alpha,w. Integration by parts gives form integral p|y_prime|^2, p=w^-2 and adjoint flux BC bar(alpha)p(0)y_prime(0)+overline(1-alpha)p(1)y_prime(1)=0. For transfer M_lambda=[[A,B],[C,D]], det=1, its boundary determinant simplifies algebraically to F_alpha=1+|alpha|^2(A-1)+|1-alpha|^2(D-1). Reflection symmetry of p gives A=D, hence F_alpha depends only on q_alpha=1/2+2|alpha-1/2|^2. The positive self-adjoint boundary problem therefore has radius-invariant spectral multiset, so do T singular values. Affinity of T in alpha and convex Ky Fan norms imply weak submajorization for increasing radii. Strict convexity of S_p (1<p<infinity), plus distinct nonzero rank-one perturbations at distinct alpha, gives strict Schatten increase. Exact unsymmetric counterexample w=sqrt(1+t) has S2^2 2/3 at alpha=0, 5/6 at alpha=1. All-rank and all-weight claims follow analytically, not from finite compressions.
